justification: Internal (staff-only) review page + write API for flagged DCP setback values: PATCH-style actions update the live dcp_setback_controls table (confirm / soft-retire / supersede-with-citation). Not public-user-facing, but it writes production regulatory rows, so Standard tier with break-it coverage of the write paths.

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_setback_controls rows flagged needs_review=TRUE by the trust sweep (13 pending rulings in Downloads/setback_decisions.csv); the /api/dcp-review verdict pattern (named reviewer + audit trail) already existed and is mirrored here.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Every action is single-row and reversible: confirm clears the flag, remove soft-retires (is_current=FALSE), fix supersedes in one transaction preserving the old row — nothing is hard-deleted, so a wrong ruling is recoverable from history.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: prior-art audited 2026-07-02: no extracted-value review WRITE API existed; this mirrors the dcp_review_queue verdict pattern but targets the versioned dcp_setback_controls rows; reviewer identity recorded in review_reason (no reviewed_by column on this table).

functions.name: POST /api/internal/setback-review/[id]
functions.input: row id plus action confirm/remove/fix with optional note and corrected values
functions.output: single-row UPDATE (confirm/remove) or transactional retire+INSERT supersede (fix) with named reviewer stamped
functions.if_none: unknown id or already-resolved row returns 404; invalid action/value/citation returns 400; DB error returns 500 with ROLLBACK — never a partial supersede

functions.name: GET /api/internal/setback-review
functions.input: no parameters — lists rows where needs_review is TRUE and is_current is TRUE
functions.output: the pending review queue rows for the internal page
functions.if_none: empty queue returns an empty list (legit-empty), DB failure surfaces as a 500 error banner, never an empty queue

values.value: body.value_min / value_max / section_ref on the fix action
values.nullable: yes — optionalNumber treats empty string, null and undefined as absent, not zero
values.guard_at: frontend-nextjs/app/api/internal/setback-review/[id]/route.ts:108 (400 unless at least one numeric bound AND a section_ref citation)
values.if_missing: the fix is rejected — no regulatory value enters the table without a source citation

queries.purpose: supersede transaction: lock the current row, retire it, insert the corrected cited row
queries.where_clause: id = $1 AND is_current = TRUE ... FOR UPDATE (single-row scope, current-row guard)
queries.if_zero: ROLLBACK and 404 — a stale/duplicate submission cannot retire an already-superseded row
queries.if_wrong: any error in the transaction ROLLBACKs both statements — history is never left retired without a replacement

break_it.scenario: Two reviewers rule on the same row concurrently (double-submit)
break_it.what_happens: The second write matches zero rows (is_current/needs_review guards + FOR UPDATE) and gets a 404, not a duplicate supersede
break_it.how: WHERE id AND is_current=TRUE AND needs_review=TRUE guards on every action; fix locks the row FOR UPDATE inside a transaction

break_it.scenario: A corrected value is submitted without a source citation
break_it.what_happens: 400 rejection — the no-value-without-citation invariant holds at the API, not just the UI
break_it.how: route returns 400 unless section_ref is non-empty and at least one numeric bound parses

break_it.scenario: The INSERT half of a fix fails after the old row was retired
break_it.what_happens: Without the transaction the value would vanish from the live table; with it the ROLLBACK restores the old row
break_it.how: BEGIN/COMMIT wraps retire+insert; catch does ROLLBACK and returns 500

break_it.scenario: value_min submitted as empty string coerces to 0 m setback
break_it.what_happens: A fabricated zero would enter a regulatory table; optionalNumber maps '' to null instead
break_it.how: optionalNumber treats ''/null/undefined as absent and non-finite as invalid

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes — open /internal/setback-review and work through the 13 pending rulings (Downloads/setback_decisions.csv); each action writes the live table one row at a time and is reversible
